card.title: Who Changed It?
card.instruction: Ask innocent questions until someone admits altering the plan, schedule, arrangement, or shared space.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can't open the cupboard. Was the sofa this close yesterday?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's more room for yoga now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Did making that room involve moving the sofa?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes, I moved it. I put the things you'll need somewhere easier.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: How thoughtful. Would those be the mugs in your sock drawer, or has someone else improved the kitchen too?

mechanism: A uses mild questions about access and misplaced objects to elicit who changed the room and kitchen arrangements.
confusable: Unlike direct accusation, A must lead B into admitting alterations through apparently innocent inquiry.
comparison: D40-b follows sofa movement into relocated mugs; D40-a remains a protected exception and is not reassessed.
provenance: Direct local assistant candidate preparation; not fresh review or acceptance.
